I am 67 years old, I never went to school, and I have farmed these six mu in Quzhou County my whole life. My husband passed away ten years ago, and my son works in the city, so it is mostly me and my daughter-in-law handling the land. I do not try new crops — I grow winter wheat and summer maize on the same fields every year because that is what my mother did, what my neighbors do, and the grain dealer comes right to the village to buy them. I cannot afford to take chances.

This year I will buy improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed from Old Wang's shop, just like last year. For wheat, I will hire the rotary tiller to prepare the soil in October because I cannot turn it myself anymore. For maize, there are only a few days between wheat harvest and planting in June, so I will plant no-tillage — I learned that rushing to plough deep just makes me miss the rain window. 

For fertilizer, I think in bags, not kilograms. On wheat, I put one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu at planting, then topdress with about one bag of urea per mu — half before winter and half at jointing when the wheat looks a little yellow. On maize, I put compound fertilizer in the planting hole and spread about half a bag of urea when the plants are knee-high. I irrigate wheat three times — winter water, jointing, and filling. Maize gets two irrigations if the sky stays dry; water costs money now, so I watch what my neighbors do. I spray wheat three times — herbicide once after emergence, and insecticide twice when I see aphids. On maize I spray twice, for weeds and corn borers. I expect about 960 jin per mu for wheat and about 1,040 jin per mu for maize if the weather holds.
